clue.text: After Sunday, the party's over-so is the dance over the border

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters behind the Sunday abbreviation
the party being over suggests it has been upended, so these letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Once Sunday comes the celebrations end, and so does a dance from north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the anagram signal on THE PARTYS, giving TRATHSPEY behind S. 'Over the border' means in Scotland, as seen from England.
explanation.definitionFit: A strathspey is a slow Scottish reel, a dance from north of the English border.

clue.text: Playwright starting to speak -speak with a drawl

indicators.note: starting to points at only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to haw is to speak hesitantly or drawlingly, as in hum and haw

explanation.surface: A dramatist begins to talk in a slow drawl.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish dramatist, author of Pygmalion.

clue.text: Bang-on-time journalistic style

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a bang is a loud report, as of a gun
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Writing that is perfectly punctual in the news trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang-on-time' reads as one idiom for punctual, but splits as Bang, on, time.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is the reporting of news, the style of factual journalism.

clue.text: Old couple producing Innocents Abroad

explanation.surface: An elderly pair turning out naive travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Innocents Abroad is a travel book by Mark Twain.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain is an archaic word for a pair, and Mark Twain wrote The Innocents Abroad.

clue.text: Sitting in court

parts.note: a sitting of judges is a period when the court is convened and hearing cases

explanation.definitionFit: A court's meeting period, during which it hears business, is a formal sitting.

clue.text: Saying that is giving energy to two farm-animals

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
a pig is one farm animal
a ram is the second farm animal

explanation.surface: A remark meaning we must feed up a pair of livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Saving', but the definition needs 'Saying'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty remark or pithy maxim.

clue.text: Fish to catch at

explanation.surface: A fish is for snatching.
explanation.walkthrough: To catch at faults is to cavil, the same as to carp at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The carp is a freshwater fish, and to carp is to find fault with niggling complaints.

clue.text: A single girl going astray

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: An unmarried girl wandering off the path.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss has gone wrong, wandering from its proper course.

clue.text: False trade-plate found in the Lake District

indicators.note: a false version is not the genuine article, so these letters are faked into a new order

explanation.surface: A forged dealer's number plate turns up in Cumbria.
explanation.walkthrough: Trade plates are temporary number plates used by motor dealers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterdale is a village near Ullswater in the Cumbrian fells of the Lake District.

clue.text: Away from shore, like nurses resting?

explanation.surface: Out to sea, as nurses on their break are.
explanation.walkthrough: Nurses off duty are off the wards.
explanation.definitionFit: Offwards is a nautical word for moving out to sea, and nurses on a break are off the hospital wards.

clue.text: Good mark in exam-a record had, almost

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut just short of its final letter

parts.note: had, verb

explanation.surface: Someone did well in a test, almost owning a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is a top grade in British school marking, an A.

clue.text: Hide at Welsh town, miser

indicators.note: at joins the two pieces side by side

parts.note: skin is an animal's hide
Flint is a town in north-east Wales

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted man hiding out in a town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a mean person who hates spending money.

clue.text: French close to row at border

parts.note: on can mean next to, as in a house on the river
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A Frenchman nearly having an argument at the edge of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the boundary line between two countries.

clue.text: Women's teas arranged for weight loss

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the following word are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Ladies lay out their afternoon tea as part of a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste is a wasting away of the body, a gradual decline in flesh and strength.

clue.text: Series of athletic events shut up by Irish radio-station endlessly

indicators.note: by sets the two pieces next to one another

parts.note: pent means confined or penned in

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Athlone was the site of the Irish national transmitter and a name on old radio dials

explanation.surface: Sporting contests silenced by an Irish broadcaster that won't stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The pentathlon is a contest of five athletic disciplines.

clue.text: There's great happiness in having toe nail treated.

indicators.note: treated suggests the toe nail is worked on and so reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A chiropodist's patient is overjoyed after attention to a sore toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of high spirits and joy.

clue.text: I'm to join political group about one, showing up inequality

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, with the group's letters going round one

parts.note: a party is a political organisation
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone joins a party only to find it unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Imparity is lack of equality or a disparity.

clue.text: but in the main she won't need it

annotationWithheld.why: 'but in the main she won't need it' as held starts mid-sentence: the opening words, and whatever 'it' refers to, are missing, and no reprint or search gives them
annotationWithheld.clue: but in the main she won't need it

clue.text: Citadel yielding a harvest on poor soil

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first part above the next

parts.note: a crop is a harvest

indicators.note: poor suggests the soil is in bad condition, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A fortress producing a crop from bad ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is a fortified hilltop citadel of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Originator of Tragedy scholarly essay, about a page

indicators.note: about means the essay wraps around the page

parts.note: a thesis is a dissertation
p is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: An academic paper on the origins of drama, wrapped round a single sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek poet Thespis is traditionally credited as the first actor and founder of tragic drama.

clue.text: Boils up parts of fricassee the second time

indicators.note: parts of tells us the answer is taken from pieces of these words

explanation.surface: A stew comes to the boil again on reheating.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of fricassee, all of 'the' and the start of 'second'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that seethes bubbles and froths as if boiling.

clue.text: Walter's dissipated-a good-for-nothing

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered, so the letters are dispersed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Walter led a dissolute life and was a waster.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is an idle spendthrift who achieves nothing.

clue.text: World's-end cry-alternative to big bang theory?

explanation.surface: The end of the world described as a scream, a rival theory to the big bang.
explanation.walkthrough: T S Eliot's The Hollow Men ends 'This is the way the world ends, not with a bang but a whimper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot's poem has the world end in a feeble cry rather than an explosion.

clue.text: Fortress is to be lofty

explanation.surface: A stronghold stands high.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower is a fortified keep, and to tower is to rise high above.

clue.text: Money earned for fares?

parts.note: a cabby or ticket collector's takings are paid for passengers carried, and the pay is the reward a worker fares with

explanation.definitionFit: Pay received for one's work is the earnings of a working week.

clue.text: Mince-pie range seen by lantern

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the letters of the next word are cut and reordered

parts.note: scope means range or extent

explanation.surface: A display of festive pastries viewed by lamplight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince' turns PIE into EPI. 'Mince-pie' reads as the Christmas pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: An episcope is a projector throwing images of opaque objects onto a screen, a kind of magic lantern.

clue.text: Small scout in charge? That's dicey!

parts.note: a cub is a junior scout

explanation.surface: A young scout put in command: that's risky!
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicey' means risky in the surface but here means like a die.
explanation.definitionFit: A die is a six-faced solid, so something dice-shaped is cube-shaped.

clue.text: Gray's collective winders?

parts.note: in Gray's Elegy the lowing cattle 'wind slowly o'er the lea', so the cattle as a group are the ones that wind

explanation.definitionFit: A group of cattle, as in Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.

clue.text: Vessel with a good beam?

parts.note: a beam is a ship's width, but here it is the shine of a lamp warning other ships

explanation.definitionFit: A moored ship with a bright lamp serves as a floating lighthouse.

clue.text: Composer taking part in tribal fetish

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musician joins in a tribal ritual object's worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Balfe was an Irish composer, best known for the opera The Bohemian Girl.

clue.text: Safe place to let out the clutch?

definitions.text: Safe place to let out the clutch?

parts.words: Safe place to let out the clutch?
parts.note: a clutch is a set of eggs, which hatch and let the chicks out in a secure spot, not a car pedal

explanation.definitionFit: A bird's home where eggs are laid and hatched is a snug refuge.

clue.text: Dress-coat I change-not wanted by one's own group

definitions.text: not wanted by one's own group

indicators.note: change means the letters are altered into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone who switches formal wear is cold-shouldered by their peers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracised people are excluded and shunned by their community.
